title: Best Gyms in Chicago (2026): 7 Verified Picks by Price, Pools and Neighborhood
meta_title: Best Gyms in Chicago (2026): Prices, Hours & Day Passes
description: 7 Chicago gyms compared: Mode Gym, Chicago Fitness Center, Chicago Athletic Clubs, The Garage, East Bank Club, Midtown and Lakeshore, with published prices, hours and day passes checked October 2026.
author: Dinesh Jeengar
author_bio: Dinesh Jeengar owns and publishes The Fitness Falcon. Articles share general information about fitness and everyday wellness; no medical qualification or clinical review is implied by this byline.
featured_image_alt: A modern gym with power racks and a loaded barbell beside floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking a dense skyline of steel-and-glass towers beside a wide blue lake
content:
The best gym in Chicago depends on how much club you want and which neighborhood you'll actually get to. For the best-value full gym with classes, Mode Gym in the West Loop is $80 to $125 a month with no enrollment fee. For the cheapest verified membership, Chicago Fitness Center in Lakeview sells six months for $294 with classes included. For a seven-club network with pools, Chicago Athletic Clubs runs a $0 enrollment promotion but doesn't publish dues online. For coached strength classes, The Garage Chicago in West Town and Lincoln Park is the pick. At the top end, East Bank Club publishes $295 a month plus a $750 initiation fee, while Midtown Athletic Club in Bucktown and Lakeshore Sport & Fitness in Lincoln Park keep their prices on request.

How this list was made: The Fitness Falcon did not visit, tour or train at any of these gyms. This is a research-based guide, rewritten in October 2026 to replace an earlier version of this page. Every gym was checked on its official website and at least one independent source on 18 October 2026. No gym paid to be included. Prices are exactly as each gym publishes them, and where a gym doesn't publish a price we say so. We don't quote star ratings or review counts. If you're weighing a national chain, our guide to US gym chain membership prices and fees compares the big names side by side.

The best gyms in Chicago, by type

Mode Gym: best-value full gym with classes

What it offers: A West Loop club at 1301 W Madison Street that lists Olympic power racks and lifting platforms, a full Hammer Strength free-weight line, Life Fitness strength and cardio machines, multiple cable towers, boxing equipment with one-on-one boxing training, a group fitness space and Styku 3D body scanning. Every membership includes unlimited group classes, three guest passes, free monthly body scans, a free personal-training session, a fitness assessment and validated parking. The site says a larger "Mode 2.0" is coming.

Published pricing (checked October 2026):

  • Annual contract paid in full: $80 a month equivalent.
  • Annual contract paid monthly: $89.95 a month.
  • Month-to-month, no contract: $125 a month.
  • $0 enrollment fee on all three. Guest passes are $40 for a full day, or complimentary for first-time local visitors.

Hours: The official site doesn't list hours. An independent listing shows Monday to Friday 5am–11pm and weekends 8am–8pm, so confirm with the gym.

Best for: People who want a serious free-weight floor plus classes, scans and parking for one mid-range price. New to the floor? Start with a simple full-body gym workout.

Honest con: The cheapest rates need a 12-month contract, there's no pool, and the site's footer still reads 2023, so some details may be stale.

Chicago Fitness Center: cheapest verified membership

What it offers: A family-owned gym at 3131 N Lincoln Avenue in Lakeview with about 40,000 square feet on two levels. The site lists cardio, resistance and functional-performance training areas, group classes, and a martial-arts dojo with an MMA cage and kickboxing ring (its Shido-kan program runs karate, kickboxing and MMA, including a children's program). Personal trainers are independent contractors who set their own rates. Metered parking is in front, with a lot behind the building.

Published pricing (checked October 2026): The membership page shows one offer: six months for $294 paid in full, with all group classes included and a $0 initiation fee. That works out at $49 a month, the lowest verified rate in this guide. Other terms aren't published online. Family, first-responder and military discounts are available.

Hours: Monday to Friday 6am–9pm; weekends 6am–6pm. The gym used to advertise 24-hour access, and some directories still say so, but the official site now lists these hours.

Best for: Budget members in Lakeview who want a classic weight room and classes without a long contract.

Honest con: It's no longer 24/7, only the six-month deal is priced online, and there's no published day pass.

Chicago Athletic Clubs: best multi-club network with pools

What it offers: Seven clubs on one membership: West Loop, Bucktown, Lakeview, Lincoln Park, Lincoln Square, Wicker Park and Evanston. The West Loop club at 1380 W Randolph Street lists a lap swim pool, a weight room, functional-training turf, cardio, weekly group classes (Pilates, yoga, cycling, Zumba, dance and swim), rowing and barre studios, luxury locker rooms, full towel service and an adjacent parking lot.

Pricing (checked October 2026): Dues aren't published online; the site shows a "$0 enrollment plus one month free" promotion through 31 October 2026 and a join-online button. Time Out Chicago reported roughly $74 to $79 a month for a single club in December 2025, and a member answer on an independent listing put a day pass at $30 with photo ID. Treat both as reported figures, not official ones.

Hours (West Loop): The club's lot hours, Monday to Thursday 5:30am–9pm, Friday 5:30am–8pm and weekends 7am–7pm, match the hours on an independent listing. Confirm with the club.

Best for: People who move around the North Side and West Loop and want a pool and towels at a mid-range price.

Honest con: You can't see dues without starting the join process, and hours aren't in the page text.

The Garage Chicago: best coached strength and conditioning

What it offers: A locally owned training gym with two locations: West Town at 2501 W Chicago Avenue and Lincoln Park at 1118 W Fullerton. Training runs through coached classes: Heavy AF (a barbell strength program in eight-week cycles built on progressive overload), Strong X (strength and power) and Hybrid (work capacity for events like HYROX). A second space, The Apartment, runs infrared yoga and kettlebell flow classes for recovery. Personal training is available. Time Out Chicago's December 2025 list describes it as a West Town gym that started in a backyard garage in 2020.

Pricing (checked October 2026): Membership prices load inside the gym's booking app rather than on the site, so treat them as on request. The first-timer offer is two weeks of unlimited classes (price shown in the app) and a $99 first personal-training session. Memberships include one guest pass a month. Policies are clear: no freezes, class packs are non-refundable, and you cancel in your account or by email at least 14 days before your next billing once any commitment is complete. Late cancellations cost $18 and no-shows $35.

Hours: Class-based; see the live schedule. Free street parking at both locations, and showers at West Town.

Best for: People who want a coach and a program rather than an open floor. If the Heavy AF cycle sounds new, our guide to progressive overload for beginners explains the idea it's built on.

Honest con: No published prices, no open-gym hours, and strict booking and no-show fees.

East Bank Club: Chicago's biggest club

What it offers: A River North landmark at 500 N Kingsbury Street with more than 350,000 square feet. The club's site lists aquatics and swim programs, basketball, boxing, team training, cycling, fitness testing, personal training and dining; Time Out Chicago describes a track, four pools and the city's largest cardio room.

Published pricing (checked October 2026): Initiation is $750 for an individual, $600 for ages 18 to 29, and $1,000 for partners with proof of marriage or domestic partnership. Monthly dues are $295 for an individual, $275 for ages 21 to 24, and $495 for partners. Children are $15 a month (ages 5 to 12) or $150 (ages 13 to 22, on a partners membership). Corporate memberships get discounted initiation.

Hours: Weekdays 5am–11pm; weekends 7am–9pm.

Best for: People who want everything, from pools and courts to restaurants, under one roof, and will use enough of it to justify the price.

Honest con: The first year costs more than $4,000 for an individual before extras, and there's no published day pass.

Midtown Athletic Club: best for tennis, pools and spa

What it offers: A Bucktown club at 2444 N Elston Avenue across two buildings. Midtown lists tennis, group fitness, training, a pool, a spa, childcare, shopping and dining, and a hotel on site. Time Out Chicago counts 16 indoor tennis courts plus pickleball courts, pools, a spa and a 55-room hotel.

Pricing (checked October 2026): Pricing on request. The "check pricing" link leads to a membership inquiry form, and no dues are shown. New-member inquiries: 773-687-7100.

Hours: Main building Monday to Thursday 5am–11pm, Friday 5am–10pm, weekends 6am–9pm. The smaller second building opens 7am.

Best for: Tennis and pickleball players, swimmers and families who want a resort-style club on the North Side.

Honest con: No published price or day pass. Time Out rates it expensive, and the second building has shorter hours.

Lakeshore Sport & Fitness Lincoln Park: best sports club for early risers

What it offers: A Lincoln Park club at 1320 W Fullerton with basketball, curling, adult and youth tennis, platform tennis, pickleball, aquatics and a swim team, group fitness, personal training, Pilates, yoga, a spa, childcare and kids' programs. A sister club at Illinois Center downtown adds a climbing wall, a golf simulator, squash and badminton.

Pricing (checked October 2026): Pricing on request through the membership office. Members get five complimentary guest passes a year, with extra passes at half price (full price $35).

Hours (Lincoln Park): Monday to Friday 4:30am–11pm; weekends 6am–9pm, the earliest weekday opening on this list. Illinois Center runs 6am–9pm weekdays and 7am–5pm weekends.

Best for: Early-morning trainers, racquet-sport players and families who want courts, pools and childcare.

Honest con: No published price, and non-members can only visit as a member's guest.

What gym memberships cost in Chicago

Among the gyms we could verify, published monthly prices run from $49 (Chicago Fitness Center's six-month deal) to $295 (East Bank Club). Four of the seven gyms don't publish dues online. The headline number is only part of the cost:

  • Initiation fees. East Bank Club charges $600 to $1,000. Mode and Chicago Fitness Center charge $0. Chicago Athletic Clubs waives enrollment during its current promotion.
  • Commitment. Mode's $80 and $89.95 rates need a 12-month contract; its no-contract rate is $125. Chicago Fitness Center's deal is six months paid up front.
  • Cancellation terms. The Garage asks for 14 days' notice and offers no freezes. Others don't publish their terms, so get them in writing.
  • Day passes. Mode's $40 guest pass (free for first-time locals) is the only official day rate on this list. Chicago Athletic Clubs' $30 pass is reported, not published.

Planet Fitness, LA Fitness, Anytime Fitness, Fitness Formula Clubs and XSport all have Chicago clubs, but none could be verified from an official page our checks could read. Our US gym chain price comparison covers the national chains' published rates and annual fees.

How to choose a gym in Chicago

  1. Start with your schedule. None of these gyms is open 24/7. Lakeshore Lincoln Park opens earliest at 4:30am, and East Bank, Midtown and Mode run to 11pm on weekdays. Class gyms like The Garage only work if the schedule fits your day.
  2. Pick a side of the city. The picks cover the West Loop (Mode, Chicago Athletic Clubs), West Town (The Garage), River North (East Bank), Bucktown (Midtown), Lincoln Park (Lakeshore, The Garage) and Lakeview (Chicago Fitness Center). In winter, the gym on your commute wins. That's general advice, not a measured finding.
  3. Check parking. Mode includes validated parking. The Garage lists free street parking at both locations. Chicago Athletic Clubs West Loop has an adjacent lot. Chicago Fitness Center has metered spots and a rear lot.
  4. Price the whole first year. Add initiation and any annual fee to 12 months of dues. East Bank Club's individual first year is $4,290 before extras; Mode's is $960 on the prepaid annual plan.
  5. Use the trial at the hour you'd train. Mode's free first visit for locals, The Garage's two-week intro and Chicago Athletic Clubs' free pass all let you see how busy the floor is. If you've been away a while, our guide to returning to the gym after a long break has a sensible first-month plan.
  6. Read the cancellation terms. Illinois law adds protections, below, but your contract's notice period still applies.

Illinois gym contract basics

Illinois regulates gym contracts under the Physical Fitness Services Act (815 ILCS 645). Section 6 gives members these rights:

  • Three-business-day cancellation. You can cancel within three business days after the first business day after you sign, for a full refund. A business day is any day the facility is open.
  • Seven days for unopened clubs. If the facility hasn't opened yet, or you didn't buy at an existing facility, you get seven calendar days to cancel.
  • Moving. If you move more than 25 miles away and the club doesn't offer a comparable facility within 25 miles, you can cancel. You owe only the charges up to the date the club gets evidence of your move, plus any contract fee capped at the lesser of 10% of the unused balance or $50.
  • Death or disability. You or your estate owe only the charges up to the date of death or the start of the disability. The club may ask for reasonable evidence.
  • Notice and refunds. Cancellation must be in writing, by certified or registered mail to the address in the contract, online through the club's website if you signed up online, or by email if the contract gives an email address. Refunds are due within 30 days of the club receiving your notice.

For federal rules and other states, see our guide to gym fees and how cancellation works.

This is general information, not legal advice. For a specific dispute, read your contract and contact the Illinois Attorney General's consumer protection division or a lawyer.

How we chose these gyms

We built this list from desk research, not visits. We didn't tour, train at or get paid by any of these gyms, and none paid to be included. We started from the gyms in the earlier version of this page and the clubs named in Time Out Chicago's December 2025 list, then kept only those whose current details we could confirm on the gym's own website and at least one independent source. We aimed for a spread of budgets and training styles: a mid-range full gym, a budget neighborhood gym, a multi-club network, a coached strength gym and three full-service clubs. For each gym we recorded what it publishes: address, hours, equipment and classes, membership and day-pass prices, and the fees that change the real monthly cost. Where a gym doesn't publish a price, we say so instead of guessing. We don't use star ratings or review counts. Everything was checked on 18 October 2026.

Two gyms from the earlier version of this page are gone. Number One Gym's web address now points to an unrelated gambling site, so we couldn't confirm it's operating. Anytime Fitness Logan Square's official club page wouldn't load for our checks, although the chain's 24/7 clubs remain an option worth checking directly. Fitness Formula Clubs, Quads Gym, XSport Fitness, the YMCA of Metro Chicago and Planet Fitness all blocked our automated checks. We'll add any of them once we can confirm details from official sources.

How we score these gyms

Each gym gets a score from 1 to 5 on five criteria, in half-point steps. The overall score is the average of the five, rounded to one decimal place. We score only what each gym publishes, as described in this guide. We did not visit, tour or train at any of these gyms, and no gym paid for its score.

When a gym doesn't publish its price, its value score is capped at 3.0, because you can't judge value without a price. A specialist gym can still score highly on facilities if its equipment is strong for what it does. These scores are a starting point for your shortlist. They are not a substitute for a trial visit at the time you'd actually train.

  • Value: the price compared with what's included, after initiation, annual and processing fees.
  • Facilities: the equipment and amenities listed, such as platforms, pools, saunas, recovery areas and studios.
  • Access: opening hours (24/7 scores highest), day passes or free trials, and the number of locations.
  • Coaching: the range of classes, coaching and programming on offer.
  • Transparency: whether prices, contract and cancellation terms, and hours are clearly published.

FAQ

What is the cheapest gym in Chicago?

Of the gyms we verified, Chicago Fitness Center's six-month membership at $294 paid in full works out at $49 a month with classes included. Mode Gym is $80 a month on a prepaid annual contract. National budget chains advertise less, but we couldn't verify their Chicago clubs for this guide.

Are there 24-hour gyms in Chicago?

None of the gyms on this list is open 24 hours. Chicago Fitness Center dropped its 24-hour schedule and now closes at 9pm on weekdays. Lakeshore Lincoln Park opens earliest, at 4:30am. Anytime Fitness runs 24/7 clubs in the city, but we couldn't verify a specific club's page.

Can I buy a gym day pass in Chicago?

Mode Gym sells a $40 full-day guest pass and gives first-time local visitors a free day. Chicago Athletic Clubs' $30 day pass is reported by a member, not published. Lakeshore admits guests only with a member. East Bank Club and Midtown don't publish a day pass.

How much is East Bank Club?

$295 a month for an individual plus a $750 initiation fee, or $275 a month for ages 21 to 24 with a $600 initiation fee for ages 18 to 29. Partners pay $495 a month plus $1,000 initiation.

Which Chicago gyms have a pool?

East Bank Club, Midtown Athletic Club, Lakeshore Sport & Fitness and Chicago Athletic Clubs (lap pools at several clubs, including West Loop). Mode, Chicago Fitness Center and The Garage don't have one.

Which is the best gym in Chicago for strength training?

For coached barbell programs, The Garage Chicago's Heavy AF cycles. For an open floor, Mode Gym lists Olympic power racks, platforms and a full Hammer Strength line.

Can I cancel a gym contract in Illinois?

Yes. Within three business days of signing (seven calendar days if the club hasn't opened), for a full refund within 30 days of the club receiving your written notice. You can also cancel if you move more than 25 miles away without a comparable club nearby, or on death or disability.
